summary: The session closed with a split tape: risk appetite returned while the macro anchor did not loosen. The total risk score eased to 43.81 (-1.51 versus the prior day), still inside caution, with the regime holding at goldilocks and model confidence at 0.9168. Relief came from volatility: VIX fell to 15.2, realized vol to 8.31, and the volatility dimension scored just 17.58; crypto warmed in sync, with BTC at 81436, ETH 2511 and SOL 105.26, each up more than 5% on the day. But leadership rotated out of hardware and into software and platforms: autos +6.57%, AI software +3.92%, enterprise software +3.57% and data centers +2.93% led, while semis leaders -0.25%, memory -1.33% and networking -1.1% lagged; at the single-name level TSLA +6.57% and NVDA +2.22% (on the Hugging Face acquisition headline) advanced, but AVGO -2.43% and MU -0.75% weighed on the hardware chain. Macro remains the hardest constraint (63.16): the 10-year Treasury rose to 4.79%, the 2-year to 4.39%, the 10-year real rate at 2.44% sits in the 99.28 percentile, and the FedWatch implied rate of 3.915% is above the 3.63% effective fed funds rate, pointing toward a hike. Policy signals are two-sided: Waller said he would consider backing a hike if inflation runs hot, while Vice President Vance publicly called for cuts (news importance 59.56 and 59.5 respectively). Inflation itself is cooling (headline CPI 3.3%, core 2.47%), yet labor data has turned negative (monthly payrolls -23 thousand, participation 61.4%), making tomorrow's employment report the real dividing line. Breadth stays the worry: only 4.52% of constituents printed new highs, 61.94% hold above the 200-day average, and semis relative performance is -18.93 percentage points. Note that the Chinese news sources (CLS, Wall Street CN) are relayed through RSSHub and are second-hand aggregation, not first-party official statements.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation sits at just 0.5 and is the single largest risk contributor (7.5 points): the dollar index at 118.75 and the 10-year real rate at 2.44% both trigger pressure signals, so the rally in risk assets is not confirmed across assets.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.79% (99.04 percentile), the 2-year to 4.39%, and the 10-year real rate at 2.44% sits in the 99.28 percentile, making macro the highest scoring dimension at 63.16 of the six.

Overnight reverse repo reads 0.702 in the 4.9 percentile, carrying a 90.21 risk score; the Fed balance sheet slipped to 6730912 and bank reserves to 2924936, so the liquidity buffer keeps thinning and the liquidity and credit dimension trend is rising.

The equity structure dimension trend is falling: only 4.52% of constituents printed 52-week highs (risk score 80.96), 61.94% hold above the 200-day average, small caps trail at -1.13 and semis at -18.93, so index gains rest on a narrow set of heavyweights.

The FedWatch implied rate of 3.915% sits above the current 3.63% effective fed funds rate, pointing toward a hike; on the same day Waller said he would consider backing a hike if inflation runs hot (importance 59.56) while Vice President Vance publicly called for cuts (importance 59.5), amplifying two-sided policy noise ahead of tomorrow's employment report.

supporting_signals.claim: Hardware clearly lagged software: memory -1.33%, networking -1.1% and semis leaders -0.25%, with AVGO -2.43%, MU -0.75% and AMD -0.05% contrasting sharply against AI software +3.92% and enterprise software +3.57%.

Labor is cracking: monthly payrolls at -23 thousand (prior 20), the drop in unemployment to 4.1% came alongside participation slipping to 61.4%, continuing claims rose to 1779000 and initial claims to 206000.

The A-share tech complex (China close) stayed split: 300475.SZ +4.65% and 688825.SH +2.26% advanced while 603986.SH -1.46%, 688008.SH -1.6% and 001309.SZ -1.91% fell, failing to track the broad gain in US software.
The trend dimension is falling: 3-month momentum is just 2.14, price sits 8.67% above its 200-day average and the 52-week drawdown is -0.59%, so upside momentum is fading rather than building.

contradicting_signals.claim: Volatility is a genuine release valve: VIX fell to 15.2 (24.21 percentile), realized vol is 8.31, and the volatility dimension scores just 17.58 with a falling trend.
Credit shows no stress: high-yield OAS at 2.66% sits in the 5.46 percentile (risk score 5.46) and investment-grade OAS at 0.81%, clearly diverging from the concerns in equity structure.

Inflation is cooling with anchored expectations: headline CPI eased to 3.3% (prior 3.46%) and core CPI to 2.47% (prior 2.57%), while the 5-year forward inflation expectation at 2.33% and the 10-year breakeven at 2.34% held steady, arguing against the hawkish pricing.
Crypto turned risk-on in sync: BTC at 81436, ETH at 2511 and SOL at 105.26, each up more than 5% on the day, so risk appetite is not contracting.

what_changed_today: The total risk score fell 1.51 from the prior day to 43.81, still inside caution.
VIX fell from 16.34 to 15.2, making volatility the day's largest source of relief.
The 10-year Treasury rose from 4.75% to 4.79% and the 2-year from 4.34% to 4.39%, with the 10Y-2Y curve holding at 0.4.
Leadership rotated: autos +6.57%, AI software +3.92%, enterprise software +3.57% and data centers +2.93% led, with memory -1.33% and networking -1.1% at the bottom.
TSLA gained 6.57% and NVDA 2.22% on the day, but AVGO -2.43% left the semiconductors theme essentially flat (+0.01%).
Overnight reverse repo rose from 0.525 to 0.702 while the Fed balance sheet declined from 6745699 to 6730912.
Waller said publicly that he would consider backing a hike if next week's inflation print runs hot, the day's second-most important story (59.56).
watch_next: Tomorrow's US employment report at 12:30Z is the core variable: monthly payrolls are already at -23 thousand, and any further weakening collides directly with the 3.915% hike pricing implied by FedWatch.
Whether the 10-year Treasury at 4.79% holds is the valuation anchor: a further rise pushing the real rate above 2.44% would transmit the macro dimension's 63.16 pressure into equity structure.
Whether the software versus hardware rotation persists: if the +3.92% lead in AI software fails to broaden into semiconductors (+0.01%) and memory (-1.33%), the breadth problem worsens.
Breadth repair: the new-highs ratio needs to recover from 4.52%, otherwise the 61.94% reading above the 200-day average can deteriorate quickly.
The PPI on 2026-09-10 and the CPI on 2026-09-11 are the policy-path checkpoints, since Waller explicitly tied the hike decision to inflation data.

bull_case.title: Bull case: cooling inflation pulls the real rate back and breadth catches up with software leadership
points: Headline CPI has eased from 3.46% to 3.3% and core CPI from 2.57% to 2.47%; if that continues, the 3.915% hike pricing from FedWatch unwinds.
Volatility and credit are already cooperating: VIX at 15.2, high-yield OAS 2.66% and investment-grade OAS 0.81% cushion valuations.
The advance is already broad: 19 of 22 sectors and themes rose, with data centers +2.93%, cloud computing +2.8% and internet platforms +2.29% spreading in tandem.

base_case.title: Base case: range-bound inside caution, no trend confirmation until the macro anchor loosens
points: The total score oscillates inside caution near 43.81, with the macro score of 63.16 offset by the volatility score of 17.58.
Cross-asset confirmation stalls at 0.5: indices grind higher without broadening, with only 4.52% of constituents at new highs.
Policy noise stays two-sided: the gap between the 3.63% effective fed funds rate and the 3.915% FedWatch implied rate will not converge before the data lands.

bear_case.title: Bear case: further labor weakness plus rising yields reverses a narrow-breadth rally
points: Monthly payrolls are already at -23 thousand with participation at 61.4%; another weak print tomorrow replaces the goldilocks narrative with growth risk.
With the 10-year at 4.79% and the 10-year real rate at 2.44% (99.28 percentile) both rising, a rally supported by only a 4.52% new-highs ratio is the most fragile.
The liquidity buffer is already thin: reverse repo at 0.702 and bank reserves at 2924936; continued balance-sheet contraction reduces the marginal bid for risk assets.
